title: Add Forward Digit Lists
statement:
Two non-negative whole numbers are stored as singly linked lists of digits, most significant digit first. So [8, 4, 1] is the number 841. No list starts with a 0 except the number 0 itself, which is [0].

Return their sum as a new list in the same format: most significant digit first, no leading zeros.

The numbers can have up to 100 digits, more than any built-in integer type holds exactly.

examples.why: 841 + 279 = 1120. The carry out of the top digit makes the answer one digit longer.
7001 + 999 = 8000. The lists have different lengths, so the digits line up from the right end, not from the head, and the carry ripples through three positions.
Adding zero must not add a leading 0.

constraints: No list starts with 0 unless it is exactly [0]
hints: Addition starts at the ones digit, but the ones digit is at the far end of each list. How can you visit digits from the end of a singly linked list?
Push each list's digits onto a stack. Popping gives you the digits from least significant up, already aligned on the right.
Build the answer from the back: each new digit node becomes the new head, pointing at the node you made before. Do not forget a final carry.

explain.intuition:
Column addition needs the digits from the right, and the two numbers must line up on the right: the ones digit of a 4-digit number goes with the ones digit of a 3-digit one. A forward list gives you the digits in the wrong order and does not tell you the length up front.

A stack fixes both. Push all digits of each list, then pop pairs: you get ones with ones, tens with tens, and so on, until both stacks and the carry are empty. Since the answer comes out ones-first too, prepend each new node to the front of the result instead of appending, and the list comes out in the right order without a reversal.
steps: Push the digits of a onto stack sa and the digits of b onto sb.
While either stack is not empty or carry > 0: pop a digit from each (0 if empty), compute sum, and set carry = floor(sum / 10).
Create a node with sum % 10, point it at head, and make it the new head.
pitfalls: Adding digits head to head. 7001 + 999 would then add 7 to 9.
Dropping the final carry: 5 + 5 must give [1, 0].
Converting the lists to numbers. Above 2⁵³ JavaScript numbers lose digits, and 100 digits is far beyond that.

solutions.title: Reverse, add, reverse back
solutions.idea: Reverse both lists so the ones digit comes first, run ordinary column addition, then reverse the result.

solutions.title: Two stacks, prepend the result
solutions.idea: Stacks hand out the digits from the right; prepending each new digit builds the answer in forward order without touching the inputs.

followups: You may not reverse the inputs and may not use a stack. Can you do it with the two lengths and recursion?
Subtract the smaller number from the larger one in the same format.
